2026-11-21.title: Every diamond has a story
2026-11-21.text: We make sure it's the true one. Follow for daily diamond knowledge.
2026-11-21.caption: Welcome to {brand}! Every day we'll share practical knowledge about diamonds, grading and certification, so you can buy and sell with confidence.

2026-11-22.label: THE 4Cs • 1/4
2026-11-22.title: Cut
2026-11-22.text: Cut is about how well a diamond's facets work with light. It drives brilliance, fire and sparkle more than any other C.
2026-11-22.caption: The 4Cs, part 1: Cut. A well-cut diamond returns light to your eye; a poorly cut one leaks it. Save this series!

2026-11-23.label: THE 4Cs • 2/4
2026-11-23.title: Colour
2026-11-23.text: White diamonds are graded on a scale from D (colourless) to Z (light yellow or brown). The closer to D, the rarer.
2026-11-23.caption: The 4Cs, part 2: Colour. Small colour differences can be invisible to the eye yet matter a lot on a report.

2026-11-24.label: THE 4Cs • 3/4
2026-11-24.title: Clarity
2026-11-24.text: From FL and IF through VVS, VS and SI to I: clarity describes the size, number and position of inclusions and blemishes.
2026-11-24.caption: The 4Cs, part 3: Clarity. Most inclusions can only be seen under 10x magnification - that's where grading comes in.

2026-11-25.label: THE 4Cs • 4/4
2026-11-25.title: Carat
2026-11-25.text: Carat measures weight, not size. One carat equals 0.2 grams (200 milligrams).
2026-11-25.caption: The 4Cs, part 4: Carat. Two diamonds of the same carat weight can look different in size depending on their cut.

2026-11-26.text: Trust, but verify. Every diamond deserves an independent report.
2026-11-26.author: {brand}
2026-11-26.caption: A certificate from an independent lab protects both buyer and seller.

2026-11-27.label: DID YOU KNOW?
2026-11-27.title: Lab-grown or natural?
2026-11-27.text: Lab-grown diamonds are physically and chemically diamond. Telling them apart from natural ones needs laboratory testing.
2026-11-27.caption: You can't tell a lab-grown diamond from a natural one by eye. That's exactly why testing and disclosure matter.

2026-11-28.title: Buying this season?
2026-11-28.text: Ask for an independent certificate before you pay.
2026-11-28.caption: Big shopping weekend? Make sure the diamond you buy is exactly what it's described as. Ask for the report.

evergreen.label: BUYER TIP
evergreen.title: Match the report to the stone
evergreen.text: If your diamond has a laser inscription on its girdle, check that the number matches the one on its report.
evergreen.caption: A report only protects you if it belongs to your diamond. Always check the details match.

evergreen.label: DIAMOND CARE
evergreen.title: Keep it sparkling
evergreen.text: Soak in warm water with a little mild soap, then brush gently with a soft toothbrush. Rinse and pat dry.
evergreen.caption: Oils and lotions dull a diamond's sparkle. A simple clean at home brings it back.

evergreen.label: DID YOU KNOW?
evergreen.title: Hard, not unbreakable
evergreen.text: Diamond is the hardest natural material, 10 on the Mohs scale - but a sharp knock can still chip it.
evergreen.caption: Hardness resists scratches, not impacts. Store diamond jewellery separately and take it off for heavy work.

evergreen.label: DID YOU KNOW?
evergreen.title: Some diamonds glow
evergreen.text: Under ultraviolet light, many diamonds show fluorescence - most often blue. It's noted on grading reports.
evergreen.caption: Fluorescence is one of the details a grading report records. Have you ever seen a diamond glow?

evergreen.label: LOOK-ALIKES
evergreen.title: Not everything that sparkles is diamond
evergreen.text: Cubic zirconia and moissanite can look similar at a glance. Proper gemmological testing tells them apart.
evergreen.caption: Simulants are common in the market. When in doubt, get it tested.

evergreen.text: Confidence comes from knowing exactly what you own.

evergreen.caption: Happy {weekday} from {brand}.
